correctness.finding: PASS. The clique-cover number is exactly h^2: the h^2 cluster-pair cliques cover, while representatives from all clusters induce K_{h,h} and any graph clique meets at most one cluster on each side. The Erdős--Faudree--Ordman cut inequality gives cp>=S-2a-b because a=h*C(r,2)<=b=h*C(s,2). For equality, optimal edge-colorings of K_r and K_s have u<=t and uniform matching sizes, so |R_c|<=|S_c| after alignment. With h>=t=chi'(K_s), the pairs (A_i,B_{i+c}) are distinct. Pairing R_c edges with S_c edges creates edge-disjoint K4s; surplus S_c edges create triangles using a fixed A_i vertex without crossing-edge collisions because each S_c is a matching; all remaining crossing edges are K2s. Every internal edge is used exactly once and the count is S-2a-b. The repository generator independently checks 90 small parameter cases and its collision logic matches the proof.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. Ning's full v1 text was retrieved after direct arXiv/OA full-text access failed. Proposition 3.1 treats only the symmetric graph (hK_k) join (hK_k) for even k, using a one-factorization and h>=k-1. The submitted edge-coloring construction genuinely extends that exact equality mechanism to unequal 2<=r<=s and to odd s with h>=chi'(K_s), using triangles to absorb unmatched internal edges. The 1988 Erdős--Faudree--Ordman result supplies the crossing-edge lower bound, and the 1985 join-to-independent-set theorem covers the r=1 boundary, but targeted searches did not locate this unequal joined-cluster formula.
